أَكْبَدُ Anything big, or large, and thick, in the middle. (L.) ―
-b2- كَبْدَآءُ A she-camel large in the middle: (L:) and in like manner, a tract of sand, رَمْلَةٌ. (L, K.) ―
-b3- أَكْبَدُ Big in the upper part of the belly: (L:) a man bulky in the middle, and therefore slow in his pace: fem. كَبْدَآءُ. (S, L, K. *) ―
-b4- Having the place of his liver rising, or prominent. (K.) ―
-b5- قَوْسٌ كَبْدَآءُ (tropical:) A bow of which the handle fills the hand: (S, A, L, K:) or, of which the part called the كَبِد is thick and strong. (L.) ―
-b6- كَبْدَآءُ (assumed tropical:) A mill that is turned with the hand: (L, K:) so called because of the difficulty, or trouble, with which it is turned. (L.) ＝
-A2- See مَكْبُودٌ. ＝
-A3- أَكْبَدُ A certain bird. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
